_comment: The toolchain that DESCRIBES bootstrap, deliberately outside it. bootstrap holds .md, .json and .bpmn and no executable code, because its README promises a Bootstrapping Agent that it needs no tools — so its shapes cannot be Zod in it. Owner, 2026-09-20: 'the zod schema should by one special exemption not be bootstrap, but bootstrap-tools', and 'bootstrap should not know zod at all (it is just generated by it in main and ghpages rendering pipeline)'. A SIBLING rather than a nested directory, because nesting would put .ts inside the tree a Bootstrapping Agent is told has none.
name: bootstrap-tools
description: Zod for the shapes bootstrap carries as plain JSON. The JSON is generated; bootstrap knows nothing of the generator.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — bootstrap-tools
assets.description: The one-way boundary this instance exists to protect — it reads and writes bootstrap, and bootstrap never imports from here — plus the two ways a Zod change silently moves a published contract: .refine() exports nothing, and z.object() is strict.

assets.title: bootstrap-tools
assets.description: Why bootstrap's schemas live outside bootstrap, and the measured reason a naive Zod port would weaken a published contract.

directories.description: The authoritative Zod source for bootstrap's two discussion documents. Generated into bootstrap/skills/discussion.*.schema.json by `bootstrap-tools:schemas`, with the `$id`s unchanged because they are a published contract. Declared as a `schemas` graph so these shapes appear in the schema viewer at all — bootstrap contributed 0 of 113 modules before this instance existed, for the two independent reasons its README gives.
